Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure matches the reported bug: when stopAtNonOption is enabled, PosixParser continues “bursting” a clustered short-option token even after encountering a non-option character, instead of stopping and treating the remainder as a single non-option argument.

How the failure occurs for testStopBursting():
- The test parses args ["-azc"] with stopAtNonOption=true and expects exactly one extra arg (the remainder after the first non-option char).
- In PosixParser.flatten(Options, String[], boolean) (lines 97–164), a token like "-azc" that is not a full option name and has length > 2 falls into the “requires bursting” path:
  - else { burstToken(token, stopAtNonOption); } (line 145).
- In burstToken(String, boolean) (lines 282–310):
  - i=1: ch="a" is a known option → tokens.add("-a"); currentOption = option "a".
  - i=2: ch="z" is NOT an option and stopAtNonOption is true → process(token.substring(i)) is invoked (line 302) with "zc".
- process(String) (lines 197–217) sees currentOption set to "a", which does not take an argument → it goes to the else branch (lines 211–216): sets eatTheRest=true, adds "--" and the remainder "zc" to tokens.
- Bug: after process(token.substring(i)), burstToken does not break out of the loop. The for loop continues:
  - i=3: ch="c" is recognized as an option → tokens.add("-c").
- Because the special “--” was already inserted before, any tokens after it (including "-c") are treated as non-option arguments. Thus the final argument list contains two entries ("zc", "-c"), whereas the test expects exactly one extra argument.

Root cause:
- In burstToken, when a non-option character is encountered and stopAtNonOption is true, the method calls process(remainder) but fails to stop further bursting. It should break immediately after processing the remainder. The missing break after process(...) at lines 300–303 causes continued bursting and incorrect tokenization, exactly as described in the bug report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
